name: P&G
summary: P&G (Procter & Gamble) hires graduates and experienced people into brand management, sales, supply chain, finance, engineering and IT roles. Its careers site describes four steps: application, one or more online assessments (such as the Peak Performance Assessment and, for some roles, an Interactive Assessment of cognitive ability), behavioural interviews and an offer. P&G says its interviews show how you connect with its Purpose, Values and Principles.
rounds: Online application with a short questionnaire
Online assessments: the Peak Performance Assessment, and for some roles an Interactive Assessment of cognitive ability
Behavioural interviews, one-on-one or panel, often a first round and a final round
looks_for: Specific examples: what you did, how you did it and the result
What motivates you and how you fit the role

questions.text: Tell me about a time you led others to a result even though you weren't in charge.
covers: The goal and why leadership was needed
What you did to bring people along
The result, with a number if you have one

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of something that was going wrong.
covers: What was going wrong and why it was easy to leave
The actions you took yourself
The outcome and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a stretching goal you set yourself and how you went after it.
covers: The goal and why it was a stretch
Your plan and how you tracked progress
Whether you hit it, and what you'd do differently

questions.text: Tell me about a time you did the right thing when nobody would have noticed otherwise.
covers: The situation and the shortcut available
What you did and why
What it cost you and what it protected

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with people who saw a problem differently from you. How did you reach a decision?
covers: The different views and why each made sense
How you built trust and found common ground
The decision and how the relationship held up

questions.text: Tell me about a new idea you came up with that improved how something was done.
covers: The old way and its problem
Your idea and how you tested it
The improvement, measured if possible

questions.text: A detergent brand's sales are flat. How would you find out why and decide what to do?
covers: Splitting the problem: fewer buyers or less buying, and which channels and regions
Looking at price, distribution, advertising and competitors
One focused plan and the measure that would show it worked

questions.text: How would you plan a promotion with a large retailer, and how would you judge whether it paid off?
covers: Agreeing goals with the retailer: sales, new shoppers, stock levels
The mechanics: discount, display, timing, forecasting supply
Judging extra sales against the cost, including sales borrowed from later weeks

questions.text: A plant is producing more defective packs than usual. How would you find and fix the cause?
covers: Containing it first: stopping bad stock from reaching stores
Data by line, shift, material batch and machine setting
A root-cause fix and checks so it stays fixed

questions.text: Estimate how many nappies are used in Bengaluru each day. Talk me through your logic.
covers: Population, share of babies, share using disposable nappies
Nappies per baby per day, stated as an assumption
A final number and a quick sense check

questions.text: How would you cut the time it takes to get products from a factory to stores without raising costs much?
covers: Mapping the steps and where time is lost
Options: better forecasts, fewer handoffs, direct deliveries, smarter stock positioning
The trade-offs and which change you'd try first

questions.text: Why P&G, and why this function?
covers: Something specific about P&G's brands or way of working
Why the function fits your strengths, with evidence
What you want to learn early on

questions.text: Which P&G brand would you like to work on, and what would you do for it?
covers: A brand you know and who buys it
One clear opportunity
Your idea and how you'd measure it

tips: Take the Peak Performance Assessment on your own, somewhere quiet; P&G says there are no right or wrong answers, so answer as you really are.
P&G uses behavioural interviews: prepare specific stories about what you did and the result, not what the team did in general.
Read P&G's Purpose, Values and Principles and be ready to show how your stories connect to them.
Use the interview to learn about P&G too; its hiring page says two-way communication starts from day one.
P&G says assessments must be done without real-time help from people or AI tools, so practise problem solving on your own.
